original_question: Give an example of a smooth projective curve X over a field of characteristic p > 0 together with a finite group action rho: G -> Aut(X) such that, for the deformation hull R(X, rho), the characteristic nu(X, rho) equals p^n for some finite n > 1.
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 3.1, in Gunther Cornelissen's contribution "Lifting an automorphism group to finite characteristic".
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the precise problem in the paper: it asks for an example, not a classification; it uses the paper's notation R(X, rho) and nu(X, rho); it places X in characteristic p > 0; and it asks for the specific intermediate finite characteristic phenomenon nu(X, rho) = p^n with n > 1 finite.
missing_details: The base field should be named k, since the paper states: let X be a smooth projective curve over a field k of characteristic p > 0.
The deformation problem is formulated over W(k), the ring of Witt vectors of k; this ambient ring is omitted in the draft.
The paper defines D(X, rho) as a functor on the category C of local Artinian W(k)-algebras with residue field k; the draft mentions the hull R(X, rho) but not the functor or category it comes from.
A lift of (X, rho) to A in C is not just an abstract deformation: it is a smooth finite-type A-scheme X' with special fiber X together with a G-action G -> Aut_A(X') lifting rho.
The paper says R(X, rho) is a prorepresentable hull in the sense of Schlessinger; the draft does not specify this.
The paper notes that D(X, rho) is actually prorepresentable when H^0(X, T_X)^G = 0, for example if g(X) >= 2; this useful scope condition is implicit in the draft.
nu(X, rho) is defined to be char(R(X, rho)), where char(R) is the positive generator of ker(Z -> R); the draft treats nu(X, rho) as if its meaning were already known.
The paper records that nu(X, rho) is always either a power of p or 0; this codomain information is omitted in the draft.

Nearby context shows that weakly ramified actions cannot produce the desired example: if (X, rho) is weakly ramified and nu(X, rho) != p, then nu(X, rho) = 0. This contextual restriction is not reflected in the draft.
refined_question: Let k be a field of characteristic p > 0, let X/k be a smooth projective curve, and let rho: G -> Aut_k(X) be an action of a finite group G on X. Let W(k) be the ring of Witt vectors of k, let C be the category of local Artinian W(k)-algebras with residue field k, and let D(X, rho) be the deformation functor sending A in C to the set of isomorphism classes of liftings of (X, rho) to A, where a lifting means a smooth finite-type A-scheme X' with special fiber X together with a G-action G -> Aut_A(X') lifting rho. Let R(X, rho) be the Schlessinger prorepresentable hull of D(X, rho), and define nu(X, rho) := char(R(X, rho)). Give an example of a group action (X, rho) such that nu(X, rho) = p^n for some finite integer n > 1.
equivalent_formulation: When H^0(X, T_X)^G = 0 (for instance if g(X) >= 2), so that R(X, rho) prorepresents D(X, rho), one can equivalently ask for an action (X, rho) such that nu(X, rho) = sup{char(A) : A in L(X, rho)} = p^n for some finite n > 1, where L(X, rho) = {A in C : there exists a lift of (X, rho) to A}, with the convention that the supremum of an unbounded chain p, p^2, p^3, ... is 0.
justification: The draft is targeting Section 3 rather than the paper's earlier conjectural material, because the notation R(X, rho) and nu(X, rho) is introduced exactly in Cornelissen's short note on lifting automorphism groups. The official problem is Problem 3.1, whose statement is essentially the same existential question as the draft. To make it stand alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the surrounding definitions from the opening paragraphs of Section 3: the Witt-vector base W(k), the Artinian category C, the deformation functor D(X, rho), the meaning of a lift, and the definition of nu(X, rho) as the characteristic of the hull. Remark 3.2 supplies an important nearby restriction: weakly ramified actions cannot yield examples with finite exponent n > 1. Remark 3.6 gives the paper's explicit reformulation of nu(X, rho) in terms of the supremum of the characteristics of Artinian lift rings when prorepresentability holds.
